Looking at this question about bifunctional transcription factors (TFs) and chromatin regulators in humans:

In molecular biology research, it has been established that a large majority of human transcription factors are not exclusively activators or repressors, but rather can function in both capacities depending on context (cell type, co-factors, promoter environment, etc.).

Studies examining the functional duality of human TFs and chromatin regulators have found that approximately 77% of them are bifunctional, capable of both activating and repressing transcription at different target genes.

[ANSWER]A[/ANSWER]
